To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the highly active catalysts for soot combustion can be prepared from cheap and abundant materials by the controllable co-reaction method.
the K-Co-Ce(0.8)O(2.0) catalysts with a high dispersion of active component Co and a high concentration of surface oxygen vacancies exhibit a high activity for soot oxidation.
the nanometre-size effect of active components on support and the formation of NO(3) can lead to a super catalytic activity for soot combustion.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis and characterisation of a new type of nanocomposite catalyst for soot combustion and the catalytic performances of the catalysts are evaluated by using a microreactor system.
the synthesis of a new kind of catalyst and the investigation of its mechanism.
the synthesis of a novel type of catalyst, which is composed of nanometre-size K-Co-Ce(0.5)O(2.5) particles dispersed on the nanometre-size CeO(2).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the nanocomposite K-CeO(1.5)-CoO catalyst is a highly active catalyst for soot combustion and it is a good candidate for practical use.

the highly dispersed active components, the size-match nanometer effect, the formation of NO(3) and the loose contact between soot and catalysts are all important factors in achieving high catalytic activity for soot combustion.
the super catalytic performances are due to the synergistic effect of K and Co on the CeO(2)-supported catalyst.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the nanometre effect is a key factor for the high catalytic activity of nanocomposite catalyst.
the size-match nanometer effect is the key to the super performance.
the nanocomposite KCo-CeO(,2) catalysts are the first example of the super active catalyst for soot combustion.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the nanocomposite K-CeO( 2)-Co catalysts are very promising for soot combustion.
the catalytic performances of the catalysts can be significantly improved by the size-match nanomaterial effect and NO(2) effect, which are very different from the conventional catalysts.
the size-match nanometer effect between CeO2 support and active components can lead to formation of NO2 and improve the catalytic activity of nanocomposite catalyst for soot combustion.
